## Story Goal

Expose the applicant's national ID on the single surface where product has approved it — the request **detail** payload — masked by default and only unmasked for the two viewers BR-16 names.

1. A pure rule function returns `"******1234"` for a 10-digit numeric ID; for malformed/short IDs it returns a fully-masked placeholder (⛔ PQ-23 variant — kept conservative so no partial digits ever leak).
2. `GET /api/v1/requests/:id` returns a new object `applicant: { id, name, nationalId }` on `RequestRecord`. `nationalId` is the raw string **only** when `viewer.id === request.applicantId` **or** `viewer.id === request.assigneeId`; in every other case it is the masked string (BR-16).
3. No other endpoint changes: `POST /api/v1/auth/login`, `GET /api/v1/auth/me`, `GET /api/v1/requests/mine`, `GET /api/v1/requests/queue`, `GET /api/v1/dashboard`, `GET /api/v1/accounts/reviewers`, and every supervisor/notification payload continue to omit `nationalId` (D-6). The dashboard and queue list items already contain no `nationalId` and must stay that way.
4. The request detail page renders `applicant.nationalId` **verbatim** as the server returns it. No client-side masking logic — the server is authoritative for BR-16.

**Not in scope:** changing `/me` or login; adding `nationalId` to any list endpoint; a supervisor "reveal" affordance; any audit log of unmasking; registration, password reset, or any UI to edit the national ID; translating the mask glyph.

## Product rules (from story)

- **Current behaviour:** no endpoint returns `nationalId`. BR-16 is not yet enforced because the ID is never emitted.
- **New behaviour:**
  - `GET /api/v1/requests/:id` returns `applicant: { id, name, nationalId }` where:
    - `nationalId` is the **raw** value when `viewer.id === request.applicantId` **or** `viewer.id === request.assigneeId` (BR-16 "except to the applicant themself and the request's assigned reviewer").
    - `nationalId` is the **masked** value in every other case the handler reaches (supervisors, other reviewers in the same department, any future viewer added by scope changes). Enforced server-side.
  - The mask (⛔ PQ-23 — intake "Masking format assumes last four digits"):
    - 10-digit numeric input → `"******" + input.slice(-4)` (six ASCII asterisks + last four digits). The glyph is ASCII `*` (U+002A); do **not** use a different Unicode star.
    - Any other input (length ≠ 10, or any non-digit character) → `"**********"` (ten asterisks). No partial reveal. Marked `// ⛔ PQ-23 variant` because the intake calls this handling "not specified".
    - `null`, `undefined`, empty string → the function **throws** `new Error('nationalId required')`; callers are expected to have a user row (the DB column is `NOT NULL`). Not a `ProblemError` — this is an invariant violation, not a user-facing problem.
  - No other endpoint changes shape. The `queue`, `mine`, `dashboard`, `reviewers`, `comments`, `notifications`, and `activity_log` payloads never include `nationalId` (D-6 extended to all read paths).

## Backend Tasks

### 1 — Masking rule

**Create file:** `app/api/rules/national-id.ts`

```ts
// BR-16 — National ID masking. ⛔ PQ-23 (display location and malformed handling).
export const MASK_GLYPH = '*';
export const MASK_PREFIX_LEN = 6;              // ⛔ PQ-23 ("******1234")
export const MASK_FULL = MASK_GLYPH.repeat(10); // ⛔ PQ-23 variant — malformed → fully masked
export const NATIONAL_ID_LENGTH = 10;           // matches 001_accounts.sql CHECK

const DIGITS_ONLY = /^\d{10}$/;

/** Return the public form of a national ID per BR-16. */
export function maskNationalId(raw: string): string {
  if (raw === null || raw === undefined || raw === '') {
    throw new Error('nationalId required');    // invariant: users.nationalId is NOT NULL
  }
  if (!DIGITS_ONLY.test(raw)) return MASK_FULL; // ⛔ PQ-23 variant
  return MASK_GLYPH.repeat(MASK_PREFIX_LEN) + raw.slice(-4);
}

export interface MaskTarget { applicantId: number; assigneeId: number | null }

/** BR-16: unmask only for the applicant themself and the request's assigned reviewer. */
export function canSeeUnmaskedNationalId(viewerId: number, target: MaskTarget): boolean {
  if (viewerId === target.applicantId) return true;
  if (target.assigneeId !== null && viewerId === target.assigneeId) return true;
  return false;
}

/** Convenience wrapper used by the request handler. */
export function presentNationalId(raw: string, viewerId: number, target: MaskTarget): string {
  return canSeeUnmaskedNationalId(viewerId, target) ? raw : maskNationalId(raw);
}
```

- Pure functions, no DB, no I/O. Covered by unit tests. Lives under `app/api/rules/` per AGENTS.md and planning-context "Conventions".
- Do **not** import from `app/api/modules/`.

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Applicant views their own request.** `viewer.id === request.applicantId` → unmasked raw. Enforced by `canSeeUnmaskedNationalId` (Task 1). Covered by test 3.
- **Assigned reviewer views the request.** `viewer.id === request.assigneeId` → unmasked raw. Enforced in Task 1. Covered by test 3.
- **Unassigned reviewer in the same department views the request** (reachable once staff detail access is added by a later story; today staff cannot call `GET /:id` because Story 10 limits applicant-only scope). The masking rule still applies: `assigneeId` is null or ≠ `viewer.id` → masked. Covered by test 4 as a forward-looking assertion.
- **Supervisor views the request.** Supervisors are **never** unmasked by BR-16 (BR-16 names only the applicant and the assigned reviewer; PQ-14 does not override this). Masked. Covered by test 4.
- **Request has no assignee yet** (`SUBMITTED`, before pick): `assigneeId = null` → `canSeeUnmaskedNationalId` returns true only for the applicant; everyone else sees masked.
- **Reassignment** (Story 13 `/:id/assign`): after reassign, the **new** assignee sees raw; the previous assignee immediately sees masked on the next fetch (the server reads `row.assigneeId` live each call). No cache invalidation needed.
- **Malformed ID in the DB** (would require bypassing the migration CHECK, e.g. a future rename or a bad seed). `maskNationalId` returns `"**********"` with no partial reveal (⛔ PQ-23 variant). Covered by unit test.
- **`nationalId` is `null`/empty** — invariant violation: `maskNationalId` throws a plain `Error`, Express replies 500 (per planning-context "Conventions"). Not a user-facing problem.
- **Unicode digits** (e.g. Arabic-Indic `٠١٢٣…`): `DIGITS_ONLY` is `/^\d{10}$/` and in JavaScript `\d` matches ASCII `0-9` only — Arabic-Indic digits fail the test and fall into the fully-masked branch. Covered by a unit test. If PQ-23 is answered to accept Arabic-Indic digits, update this one regex and the test.
- **Response-shape regression on other endpoints.** A regression test re-asserts that `POST /api/v1/auth/login`, `GET /api/v1/auth/me`, `GET /api/v1/requests/mine` do **not** include `nationalId` (D-6 preserved).
- **BR-18 unchanged.** This story adds no new authorization paths. If `assertOwnsRecord` or `requireRole` would already have rejected the viewer, they still do; the masking rule only shapes payloads for callers who are already allowed to read the request.
- **Logging.** Do **not** `console.log` the raw `nationalId` from any new code (no logging is added in this story).

## Migration / Rollback

- **Forward:** no DB migration. Backend adds one rule file, one repository helper, and one field on one response. Frontend adds one optional field and one render line.
- **Rollback on failure:** delete `app/api/rules/national-id.ts`, revert the three edits in `app/api/modules/requests/requests.routes.ts`, `app/api/modules/accounts/users.repository.ts`, and `app/web/src/api/requests.ts` + `app/web/src/pages/RequestDetailPage.tsx`. No data to clean up (the raw value lives only in `users.nationalId`, which already exists).
- **Half-applied state:** if the backend ships but the frontend does not, the detail page simply ignores the extra field. If the frontend ships but the backend does not, `record.applicant` is `undefined` and the header block is skipped (the optional field guard in Task 9).
